name: 46703-longprefill-70b-8gpu
hardware: 8x H100 80GB HBM3, one a3 node (--gres=gpu:8), NVSwitch, driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: TP=8, PP=1, DP=1, EP=none -- one tensor-parallel group over all eight cards of one node. Sequence parallelism is a compilation pass on top of that group, not a separate parallel axis, and does not change the world size.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=32, bounded at 320 requests with 10% warmup and 10% cooldown, leaving 256 measured; the cooldown is `mode: requests`, not guidellm's default transient mode.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, no shared prefix, prefix caching off. Prompt EXACTLY 8000 tokens (min = max = 8000) and output EXACTLY 64 (min = max = 64), with `ignore_eos` forced by the backend, so every request has an identical shape. Sampling is random (`temperature: 1.0` in `spec.backend.sampling_params`).
purpose: A document analysis assistant summarizing 8000-token reports for 32 concurrent users on one eight-GPU node.
launch:
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 8
dtype: bfloat16

# INLINE JSON, NOT A BLOCK MAP. DO NOT RE-FLOW THIS LINE: the engine's own config reader is a
# flat line reader that skips indented lines, so the block form parses to nothing, the key never
# reaches the engine, and the run proceeds silently at rc=0 without the pass.
compilation-config: {"pass_config": {"enable_sp": true}}

max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# 8448 rather than an exactly-fitting 8064: the prompt is rendered through the tokenizer's chat
# template, which costs a few dozen tokens on top of the 8000 the dataset declares.
max-model-len: 8448

max-num-seqs: 32

# 0.80 rather than 0.95, because a recurring minority of a3 nodes come up with ~13 GiB already
# held and report ~68.8 of 79.19 GiB free; 0.95 asks for 75.23 GiB and every one of the eight
# ranks then refuses at construction with "Free memory on device ... is less than desired GPU
# memory utilization". It costs the measurement nothing: the KV pool is non-binding at either
# setting. Per GPU a token costs 2 x 80 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 x 2 B / 8 ranks = 40 KiB, and
# the batch can hold at most max-num-seqs 32 x max-model-len 8448 = 270k tokens = 10.3 GiB,
# against roughly 41 GiB left after 17.6 GiB of weights and activations at 0.80. The batch stays
# bound by max-num-seqs either way and nothing is ever preempted.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.80

enable-prefix-caching: false

# Weight VALUES do not enter this measurement and reading them does not fit the run window.
# 141 GB of bf16 across 30 safetensors shards is ~570 s of reading at the front of EVERY run on
# this cluster, and on top of that this setup pays torch.compile over 80 layers in two compile
# ranges plus graph capture; the harness kills a run that has served nothing after 900 s, which
# is what happened to both sibling items on this same checkpoint. Every tensor shape, the layer
# count, the KV pool and the batch composition are identical under dummy, and guidellm forces
# `ignore_eos` with max_tokens = 64, so every request still returns exactly 64 output tokens.
load-format: dummy
